question.prompt: Find the number of pairs \((m,n)\) of integers which satisfy the equation \[ \begin{aligned} m^3+6m^2+5m &=27n^3+9n^2\\ &\quad+9n+1. \end{aligned} \]

solutions.explanation:
The coefficients 27 and 9 on the right suggest examining remainders upon division by 3. To expose the corresponding structure on the left, rewrite it as
\[
m^3+6m^2+5m
=(m-1)m(m+1)+6m(m+1).
\]
Among the three consecutive integers \(m-1,m,m+1\), at least one is divisible by 3. Their product is therefore divisible by 3, and so is \(6m(m+1)\). Thus the entire left side is divisible by 3 for every integer \(m\).

For every integer \(n\), the right side is
\[
9(3n^3+n^2+n)+1,
\]
which has remainder 1 upon division by 3. The two sides can never be equal. This excludes every integer pair, so the number of pairs is \(\boxed{0}\), choice A.
solutions.title: Compare divisibility by 3
